Announcement

Introducing the 2027 SPARK Foundation Program

Beginning in February 2027, SPARK will admit a selective cohort of Grade 9 and 10 students to a year-long program of monthly sessions running through December. Entrance examinations will be held on December 19, 2026 and in January 2027. The program is free of charge.

About SPARK

A student-led foundation for mathematical excellence.

SPARK Math Foundation prepares motivated secondary students for advanced mathematics through rigorous instruction, sustained practice, and competition.

Founded in Coquitlam, British Columbia, SPARK began as a series of open problem-solving sessions and has grown into a structured program with its own annual competition. Our instruction centres on the reasoning tested by national contests, including those set by the University of Waterloo's Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC).

SPARK is organized and taught by students, and all of its programming is offered free of charge.

2027 Foundation Program

A selective, year-long program of study.

The Foundation Program meets monthly from February to December 2027, excluding the summer break. Each session builds from foundational technique to advanced, contest-level problems.

Course Outline

The 2027 curriculum, month by month.

Each monthly session covers one subject area. The first half establishes the foundational technique; the second half extends it to advanced, contest-level problems.

MonthSubjectFoundationsAdvanced
February

Algebra

Foundations

Factoring identities, difference of squares and cubes, expressions such as x + 1/x

Advanced

Vieta's formulas, strategic substitution, telescoping sums

March

Number Theory

Foundations

Divisibility, primes, GCD and LCM, digit problems

Advanced

Modular arithmetic, last-digit problems, Fermat's Little Theorem

April

Geometry

Foundations

Angle chasing, similar triangles, area ratios

Advanced

Circle theorems, cyclic quadrilaterals, power of a point

June

Combinatorics & Probability

Foundations

Permutations, combinations, complementary counting

Advanced

Stars and bars, inclusion–exclusion, the pigeonhole principle, expected value

September

Sequences & Series

Foundations

Arithmetic and geometric sequences and their sums

Advanced

Recursion, infinite series, telescoping series

October

Inequalities & Optimization

Foundations

Properties of inequalities, maximum and minimum problems

Advanced

The AM–GM inequality, Cauchy–Schwarz, symmetric expressions

November

SPARK Competition

The annual SPARK Mathematics Competition

Cohort members compete alongside students from across the Tri-Cities

December

Final Assessment

A cumulative assessment of the year's material

Closing ceremony and Certificates of Completion

Monthly problem sets

Each session ends with a take-home problem set, submitted with written solutions at the next session.

Contest alignment

Spring topics prepare students for the CEMC Pascal and Cayley contests in February and the Fryer and Galois contests in April.

Certificate of Completion

Awarded to students who attend every session and complete the year's problem sets and final assessment.

Admissions

Admission to the 2027 cohort.

Admission is determined by a written entrance examination, offered at two sittings. Candidates sit the examination once. Admitted students commit to attending every monthly session.

  1. Open now

    Registration

    Register online for the December sitting. Examination details are sent to every registered candidate.

  2. Sat, Dec 19, 2026

    First Entrance Examination

    The first sitting of the written problem-solving examination.

  3. January 2027

    Second Entrance Examination

    A second sitting for candidates unable to attend in December. Date to be announced.

  4. Late Jan 2027

    Admission decisions

    Offers of admission are sent to candidates and families after the second sitting.

  5. February 2027

    Program begins

    The cohort holds its first monthly session.

  6. Jul – Aug 2027

    Summer break

    No sessions are held. Instruction resumes in September.

  7. December 2027

    Program concludes

    The cohort completes its year of study.

FAQ

Frequently asked questions

For anything not covered here, write to sparkmathfoundation@gmail.com.

Who may sit the entrance examination?

Students in Grade 9 or 10 who wish to join the 2027 cohort. Candidates register in advance through the online registration form.

When is the entrance examination?

The first sitting is on Saturday, December 19, 2026. A second sitting will be held in January 2027 for candidates who cannot attend in December. Each candidate sits the examination once.

Is there a fee?

No. SPARK is student-led, and all of its programming, including the entrance examination and the Foundation Program, is free of charge.

Is attendance required?

Yes. Admitted students commit to attending every monthly session from February to December 2027.

What does the examination cover?

The examination assesses mathematical reasoning and problem solving rather than memorized procedures. Details are sent to each registered candidate.

When does the program run?

Once a month from February to December 2027. No sessions are held during the summer break in July and August. The full schedule is shared with admitted students.

Do I need prior contest experience?

No. The program is designed to build contest skills over the course of the year.
